title: Fix Community Medicine visibility across all app sections

requirements.text: Ensure Community Medicine is recognized as a distinct subject in the frontend subject definitions (frontend/src/domain/subjects.ts) with all its class types (Theory, Practical, etc.) properly enumerated, matching the same structure used by Anatomy, Physiology, and Biochemistry.

quotes: its added in time table section with other subjects but in other sections it's not showing community medicine as different subject

acceptanceCriteria: Community Medicine appears as a selectable subject in the subjects list used throughout the app.
Community Medicine has the same class type options (e.g., Theory, Practical) available as other subjects.
The subject definition in subjects.ts includes Community Medicine with proper category mappings (Theory/Practical thresholds).

requirements.text: Fix the Dashboard page (frontend/src/pages/DashboardPage.tsx) to display a SubjectStatsCard for Community Medicine alongside Anatomy, Physiology, and Biochemistry, so attendance statistics for Community Medicine are visible and up to date.

quotes: I cannot mark its attendance in dashboard tab kindly fix

acceptanceCriteria: A SubjectStatsCard for Community Medicine is rendered on the Dashboard.
The card shows correct attended/conducted counts and attendance percentage for Community Medicine.
The card reflects the same threshold rules (75% Theory, 80% Practical) as other subjects.

requirements.text: Fix the Today's Schedule section on the Dashboard (frontend/src/components/TodaySchedule.tsx) and the Add Class page (frontend/src/pages/AddClassPage.tsx) so that Community Medicine timetable entries appear in today's schedule and Community Medicine can be selected as a subject when manually adding a class log.

quotes: I cannot mark its attendance in dashboard tab kindly fix
in other sections it's not showing community medicine as different subject

acceptanceCriteria: Community Medicine timetable entries scheduled for today appear in TodaySchedule with Present/Absent action buttons.
Community Medicine is listed as a selectable subject in the Add Class form.
Marking attendance for a Community Medicine class log correctly updates attendance statistics.

requirements.text: Ensure Community Medicine is available as a filter option in the Records page (frontend/src/pages/RecordsPage.tsx) and appears correctly in the Analytics page (frontend/src/pages/AnalyticsPage.tsx) subject-wise statistics.

quotes: in other sections it's not showing community medicine as different subject

acceptanceCriteria: Community Medicine appears in the subject filter dropdown on the Records page.
Records logged under Community Medicine are retrievable by filtering for that subject.
Analytics page shows Community Medicine in the per-subject attendance breakdown chart.

requirements.text: Audit the storage models (frontend/src/storage/models.ts) to confirm that the ClassLog and TimetableEntry subject type unions include 'Community Medicine' as a valid literal, and update them if missing so that storing and retrieving Community Medicine records works correctly.

quotes: in other sections it's not showing community medicine as different subject

acceptanceCriteria: The Subject type union in models.ts includes 'Community Medicine'.
TimetableEntry and ClassLog records with subject 'Community Medicine' can be stored and retrieved without type errors.
No TypeScript type errors arise from using Community Medicine as a subject value.

constraints: Do not alter the immutable frontend paths: frontend/src/hooks/useInternetIdentity.ts, frontend/src/hooks/useActor.ts, frontend/src/main.tsx, frontend/src/components/ui.
Do not change existing attendance threshold logic (75% Theory, 80% Practical).
Backend data structures already include Community Medicine — do not remove or rename existing backend entries.
nonGoals: Adding new subjects beyond Community Medicine.
Redesigning the UI layout or visual theme.
Changing the backend actor schema or migration logic.
Modifying AETCOM-specific logic unless it directly blocks Community Medicine attendance tracking.
